stem: In a closed population of 1,000 people, 100 have a condition on January 1. During the year, 45 initially unaffected people develop the condition, and 20 of the original cases recover. These are the only recoveries; no one dies or leaves. Which of the following gives the year-end point-prevalence numerator and the number of incident cases during the year?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Year-end existing cases are 100 original cases minus 20 recoveries plus 45 new cases, giving 125. Incident cases count the 45 new occurrences during the specified year.
options.misconception: No misconception: current cases account for recoveries; incidence counts new onset.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Adding the original and new cases gives 145 people who had the condition at some time during the year. Point prevalence at year end excludes the 20 who have recovered.
options.misconception: Includes recovered people in the year-end point-prevalence count.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The point-prevalence numerator is correct, but incident cases exclude people who already had the condition at the start. Only the 45 newly affected people contribute to incidence.
options.misconception: Treats all year-end existing cases as new cases during the year.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Year-end point prevalence must reflect both new cases and recoveries rather than retain the original count. Incident cases count new disease occurrences, so recoveries are not subtracted from the 45.
options.misconception: Ignores prevalence changes and incorrectly subtracts recoveries from incidence.

options.label: E
options.explanation: The 45 new cases are only part of the year-end existing caseload. The 100 people already affected on January 1 are not new cases during the year.
options.misconception: Excludes persisting old cases from prevalence while adding them to incidence.

context:
Learning objective: Distinguish new cases in an interval from all cases still present at a specified time.

Year-end existing cases are 100 original cases minus 20 recoveries plus 45 new cases, giving 125. Incident cases count the 45 new occurrences during the specified year.
